column1: # nested-run-targets.tsv -- calibrated UI target table for scripts/nested-run.sh's
# COLUMNS (tab-separated): name  lang  kind  index  x  top_y  bottom_off  probe_dx  probe_dy  state
#   name        the target's identifier, passed to `click-target NAME`
#   lang        fr | en -- the recorded launch language this row applies to
#   index       for kind=combo: the 0-based item index (Home, then Down x
#   x           LOGICAL x (px at GDK_SCALE 1) of the click point
#   top_y       LOGICAL y of the click point when the page is scrolled to
#               TOP, or "-" if the target is not visible from the top
#   bottom_off  distance in LOGICAL px from the WINDOW'S BOTTOM EDGE to the
#               click point when the page is scrolled to BOTTOM, or "-" if
#               not visible from the bottom. click_y = (window bottom) -
#   probe_dx/dy offset from the click point (x, top_y or the bottom-derived
#               y) that `check-layout` samples a single pixel at, to read
#               ACCENT/NEUTRAL without landing on a switch's white thumb or
#   state       the live config.toml key this target's state reflects
#               radio: compared against `engine`), or "-" for combo rows
#               (Strength/Mode have no simple accent/neutral pixel state).
# UNITS: window 420 px wide, harness device cmtest_mic, Khip absent (its row
# is insensitive and deliberately has no target here). All numbers below were
# measured with PIL against real screenshots taken via `nested-run.sh shot`
# at GDK_SCALE 1 on a 520x960 Xephyr (`scripts/e2e/README.md` documents the
# WHY BOTTOM_OFF DIFFERS BY LANGUAGE ONLY FOR SOME ROWS: DPDFNet-8's subtitle
# wraps to 3 lines in fr vs 2 in en, shifting every row's distance from the
# TOP by a constant amount from DPDFNet-8 onward, and every row's distance
# from the BOTTOM by that same amount for rows ABOVE DPDFNet-8's wrap point.
# Rows AFTER the wrap point (Strength/Mode/Levels/Settings) keep an IDENTICAL
# bottom_off in both languages, because nothing below them differs by
# language; enable/RNNoise (before the wrap point) keep an identical top_y.
# RECALIBRATING after a layout change: for each lang, `nested-run.sh xephyr
# :47 bottom`, `shot :47 FILE`, then read pixel colors with PIL (or the Read
# tool) to find each row's center and re-derive top_y/bottom_off exactly as
# above. Re-run `check-layout` afterward; DRIFT means a number here is stale.
